A Python 3.11 service under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service depends on roughly thirty distributions
installed into $EPISODE_ROOT/site-packages. During an egress review several
outbound connection attempts were seen going to hosts that are not the organisation's
internal mirror and appear nowhere in the first-party source under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/src; the

trusted builds of the organisation's own packages, a CycloneDX SBOM is at
$EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/sbom.cdx.json, local modifications the platform team has approved are
recorded in $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/PATCHES.md, and each installed distribution carries a dist-info
RECORD integrity manifest.

More than one distribution has been compromised through the supply chain, and they were
not all compromised the same way. Some other distributions in the environment look
irregular but are benign, and those must not be reported as compromised.

Write a findings report as a single JSON object at the absolute path $EPISODE_ROOT/app/report.json
with exactly one key, "compromised", whose value is a JSON array holding one object per
genuinely compromised distribution and nothing else. Each object must have these keys:
  package   - the distribution name
  vector    - the compromise mechanism, one of: tampered-file, malicious-wheel,
              dependency-confusion, typosquat, install-hook
  trigger   - when the injected code first runs, one of: import, install,
              runtime-entrypoint, interpreter-startup
  cwe       - the CWE identifier (form "CWE-###") that most precisely classifies the
              weakness
  owasp     - the OWASP Top 10 2021 category identifier (form "A##:2021")
  indicator - the primary indicator of compromise recovered from disk: the
              fully-qualified host the code contacts where it beacons, otherwise the
              single most specific artefact identifying the compromise (a malicious
              version string, an impersonated package name, or the module executed at
              startup)

Then remediate the environment so that every compromised distribution is neutralised —
restored to its trusted build, repinned to the trusted source, or removed — while the
benign distributions are left in place and the service under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service still imports
and runs unchanged. The environment has no outbound network access; recover every
reported value from the files on disk alone.

Report written to `app/report.json`; environment remediated and verified.

## Nine compromised distributions, five distinct vectors

| Package | Vector | Trigger | CWE | Beacon host |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| geoindex | tampered-file | import | CWE-506 | sync-metrics.geoindex-cdn.net |
| logkit | malicious-wheel | import | CWE-506 | logkit-metrics.telemetry-cdn.net |
| metricslib | malicious-wheel | import | CWE-506 | collector.metricslib-telemetry.io |
| svc-cli | malicious-wheel | runtime-entrypoint | CWE-506 | svc-cli-collect.pkg-telemetry.net |
| corp-telemetry | dependency-confusion | import | CWE-829 | corp-telemetry-public.s3-collector.net |
| metrics-core | dependency-confusion | import | CWE-829 | metrics-core-public.collector-cdn.net |
| sluglfy | typosquat | import | CWE-507 | sluglfy-collect.pkgcdn.net |
| urllib33 | typosquat | import | CWE-507 | urllib33-telemetry.pkgcdn.net |
| buildtools-ext | install-hook | interpreter-startup | CWE-506 | bt-ext-beacon.buildcdn.net |

All nine are `A08:2021` (Software and Data Integrity Failures).

**How each was separated.** `geoindex/_grid.py` is the only payload whose RECORD hash *disagrees* with disk (677→1146 bytes) — post-install edit. `logkit`, `metricslib`, `svc_cli` and `buildtools_ext` all hash-match their RECORDs, so the manifests were generated from already-backdoored content — the wheels themselves. `corp-telemetry` and `metrics-core` are marked "internal index only" in the lock, yet carried `INSTALLER: pypi-public` and version `9.9.9` against mirror builds of 1.4.2/2.0.0 — classic version-inflation confusion. `sluglfy`/`urllib33` appear in neither the lock nor the SBOM, are `pypi-public`, and shadow `slugify`/`urllib3`, which are both installed and clean. `buildtools_ext_autoload.pth` was the only file on disk in no RECORD at all — dropped by an install hook, and it accounts for the log's pre-import connection.

**Ruled benign, left untouched:** `crashreporter` and `debug_shell` (127.0.0.1 only, the latter off without `DEBUG_SHELL_ENABLE=1`), `fastserialize` (execs local first-party codec files), `vendored_min` (base64 blob decodes to a two-line CSV splitter), `oldcrypto` (SBOM CVE, not tampered), `localpatch_ui` (RECORD mismatch pre-approved in PATCHES.md — deliberately left mismatching).

## Remediation

Restored from `/opt/mirror`: `geoindex/_grid.py`, all of `logkit`, `metricslib` (injected `_agg.py` deleted). `corp-telemetry` and `metrics-core` repinned to the mirror builds with dist-info renamed to 1.4.2/2.0.0 and `INSTALLER` back to `internal-mirror`, matching the lock. The `.pth` and `_bootstrap.py` removed from `buildtools-ext`. Affected RECORDs regenerated; no `pypi-public` installer remains.

Two cases had no mirror build. `svc_cli/_hooks.py` was rebuilt as an inert `main()` returning 0, keeping the `svc-report` entry point and the lock pin intact. For the typosquats I did **not** delete the distributions: `src/svc/shim.py` imports `sluglfy` and `src/svc/net.py` imports `urllib33`, and you asked that the service run unchanged — so I stripped both payloads and reduced each package to an alias re-exporting `slugify`/`urllib3`. That is a holding measure; the real fix is repointing those two first-party imports and then uninstalling the aliases, which I noted as follow-up in PATCHES.md since it requires editing the service.

Verified with `socket.create_connection` and `socket.socket.connect` patched to raise: `svc.main.run()` returns `9q9hyh053`, `shim.norm` works, all benign packages still import, and nothing attempts an outbound connection.
